page_hint: Section 5, Common Mistakes, fifth bullet (Overlooking protocol overhead)
quoted_clause: [DERIVED: 64/66 line code plus framing/FEC overhead] attached to '~180 Gb/s' for a '200 Gb/s RoCEv2 link'
observed: The DERIVED label cites 64/66 line code as the derivation basis for the ~180 Gb/s figure, but the same paragraph explicitly states that 200GbE (802.3ck) uses 256b/257b block coding, not 64b/66b. The stated derivation basis contradicts the paragraph's own line-coding claim for 200GbE.
correction: Either (a) change the DERIVED label to cite 256/257 block coding (matching the paragraph's 802.3ck claim), recompute with RS(544,514) FEC + framing, and adjust ~180 to the recomputed value (~184 Gb/s); or (b) explicitly scope the 200GbE figure to 802.3bs (64/66) variants and note that 802.3ck variants use 256/257. The NDR InfiniBand ~380 Gb/s figure in the same bullet is correct (400 × 64/66 ≈ 388, minus protocol overhead ≈ 380) and needs no change.
acceptance_test: The DERIVED label's stated line-coding basis matches the paragraph's own claim about which encoding 200GbE uses, and the ~180 Gb/s figure is arithmetically consistent with that stated basis.
verdict_evidence: chapter-09.md §5 'Overlooking protocol overhead': '200GbE and 400GbE (802.3ck) use 256b/257b block coding before FEC, while InfiniBand HDR and NDR both use 64b/66b ... a 200 Gb/s RoCEv2 link delivers ~180 Gb/s ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED: 64/66 line code plus framing/FEC overhead]' — the single trailing label cites 64/66 for the RoCEv2 figure the same paragraph attributes to 256b/257b Ethernet coding (200×64/66 = 193.9 vs 200×256/257 = 199.2 before FEC/framing).
fix_instruction: Split the trailing derivation label so the InfiniBand ~380 Gb/s figure keeps '[DERIVED: 64b/66b line code plus framing/FEC overhead]' and the RoCEv2 ~180 Gb/s figure gets its own label citing 256b/257b block coding plus the Ethernet FEC/framing overhead.

quoted_clause: Latency column: '~us' for GPU-to-GPU (NVLink), GPU-to-CPU/NIC (PCIe), Node-to-node (RoCE/Ethernet), and Rack/cluster (InfiniBand) rows
observed: All four network-layer rows show '~us' in the Latency column, making NVLink, PCIe, RoCE/Ethernet, and InfiniBand appear identical in latency. The chapter's opening paragraph claims 'Each layer still has a distinct bandwidth ceiling, a distinct latency profile, and a distinct cost per gigabyte,' but the table's latency column communicates no distinction among network layers.
correction: Replace '~us' with representative ranges that distinguish layers: NVLink '~1–2 μs', PCIe '~1–2 μs', RoCE/Ethernet '~2–10 μs', InfiniBand '~1–5 μs', each tagged [ILLUSTRATIVE] if not 1P. Alternatively, add a brief note under the table: 'All network layers are microsecond-class but differ by roughly an order of magnitude; the bandwidth column is the primary differentiator in this table.'
acceptance_test: A reader can see from the table that network-layer latencies differ meaningfully, consistent with the chapter's claim of 'a distinct latency profile' per layer.
verdict_evidence: chapter-09.md Table 9-1: rows 'GPU-to-GPU (in-node) | NVLink (H100) | ... | ~us', 'GPU-to-CPU / NIC | PCIe Gen5 | ... | ~us', 'Node-to-node (rack) | RoCE / Ethernet 400Gb/s | ... | ~us', 'Rack/cluster | InfiniBand HDR/NDR | ... | ~us' — four network layers share one latency value (first three tagged [1P][FACT]) while §1 asserts 'Each layer still has a distinct bandwidth ceiling, a distinct latency profile, and a distinct cost per gigabyte'.
fix_instruction: Give the four network rows distinguishing latency ranges (e.g. NVLink ~1–2 μs, PCIe ~1–2 μs, RoCE/Ethernet ~2–10 μs, InfiniBand ~1–5 μs) tagged [ILLUSTRATIVE], or add a footnote under Table 9-1 stating that all four network layers are microsecond-class and only the order of magnitude is specified.

quoted_clause: 'each per-layer all-reduce is ~0.45 MB sent per rank — batch × hidden × bytes'
observed: The formula 'batch × hidden × bytes' computes the logical tensor size, but the phrase 'sent per rank' implies physical network traffic. The chapter explicitly distinguishes these in §9.1: 'The 140 GB is a logical input size, not the physical traffic of the collective.' For a ring all-reduce with N ranks, physical send volume per rank is 2(N−1)/N × tensor_size (1.75× for N=8). The mini-case presents the logical size as 'sent per rank,' contradicting the chapter's own terminology distinction. Additionally, the downstream claim 'the tens of MBs... is the per-step total across all 80 layers' is ambiguous: 0.45 × 80 = 36 MB (logical, 1 all-reduce/layer) vs 0.79 × 80 = 63 MB (physical ring, 1/layer) vs 126 MB (physical ring, 2/layer — standard Megatron-style TP has 2 all-reduces per layer: after attention and after MLP). 126 MB is not 'tens of MBs.'
correction: Change to 'each per-layer all-reduce operates on a ~0.45 MB tensor (batch × hidden × bytes)' — removing 'sent per rank.' For the total, state the basis explicitly: 'the logical tensor volume across all 80 layers is ~36 MB (1 all-reduce/layer) to ~72 MB (2/layer)' or provide the physical traffic figure with the ring factor stated. Specify the all-reduces-per-layer count. Ensure the basis (logical vs physical) is consistent with §9.1's distinction.
acceptance_test: The mini-case's per-layer figure is labeled as either logical tensor size or physical traffic, consistent with §9.1's terminology; the all-reduces-per-layer count is stated; and the 'tens of MBs' total is derived from a stated basis that arithmetically yields a value in the 'tens of MBs' range.
verdict_evidence: chapter-09.md §8 mini-case: 'each per-layer all-reduce is ~0.45 MB sent per rank — batch × hidden × bytes', while §9.1 of the same chapter states the convention this breaks: 'The 140 GB is a logical input size, not the physical traffic of the collective. For an eight-rank point-to-point ring, each rank sends 245 GB and receives another 245 GB' (2(N−1)/N factor).
fix_instruction: In the Ch 9 §8 mini-case, call 0.45 MB the logical per-layer activation tensor ('each per-layer all-reduce operates on a ~0.45 MB tensor — batch × hidden × bytes'); if a per-rank traffic figure is wanted, apply the chapter's 2(N−1)/N convention, and state whether the ~36 MB across 80 layers is logical volume or physical traffic.

page_hint: Section 7, What We Still Don't Know, third bullet (Optical interconnects)
quoted_clause: 'optical intra‑rack fabrics (400 Gb/s–800 Gb/s per lane) are entering data centers'
observed: 'Per lane' is ambiguous (wavelength? electrical lane? fiber pair? module aggregate?) and the upper end (800 Gb/s per lane) overstates current deployment readiness. As of 2026, mainstream optical lane rates are 100–200 Gb/s PAM4; 400 Gb/s per single wavelength/lane is in early development; 800 Gb/s per lane is research-stage. The present-tense 'are entering' implies deployment readiness for the full 400–800 range.
correction: Define 'lane' explicitly and scope the tense: e.g., 'optical modules at 400–800 Gb/s aggregate are entering data centers, with per-lane (per-wavelength) rates of 100–200 Gb/s deployed today and 400 Gb/s per lane in development.' Or: 'lane rates of 100–200 Gb/s are deployed, with 400 Gb/s per lane under development and higher rates in research.'
acceptance_test: The term 'lane' is defined, and the claimed rates are consistent with the deployment stage implied by the verb tense.
verdict_evidence: chapter-09.md §7 bullet 'Optical interconnects and the next generation': 'optical intra‑rack fabrics (400 Gb/s–800 Gb/s per lane) are entering data centers' — no evidence label, 'per lane' undefined, and 800 Gb/s is a module aggregate rate, not a lane rate (retrieved source: '800G DR8 = 8 lanes × 100G PAM4').
fix_instruction: Define 'lane' and scope the rate to what ships: e.g. 'optical modules at 400–800 Gb/s aggregate are entering data centers, with per-lane (per-wavelength) rates of 100–200 Gb/s deployed today and 400 Gb/s per lane in development', and tag the claim [ILLUSTRATIVE] or [1P: vendor datasheet].

quoted_clause: In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r.
observed: The caption states that the same chunk-index formula applies in both reduce-scatter and all-gather, and that rank r ends reduce-scatter holding chunk r. In the standard balanced ring all-reduce, reduce-scatter and all-gather use different chunk indices. With 0-indexed rounds, rank r ends reduce-scatter holding chunk (r+1) mod N; all-gather then sends chunk (i−r+1) mod N at round r. With 1-indexed rounds, the reduce-scatter formula can be made to leave rank r holding chunk r, but the all-gather formula is still not the same as the reduce-scatter formula.
correction: State the two phase-specific formulas explicitly, or re-index rounds and chunks so that the figure's arrows and the caption agree. For 0-indexed rounds: reduce-scatter sends chunk (i−r) mod N; all-gather sends chunk (i−r+1) mod N. For 1-indexed rounds: reduce-scatter sends chunk (i−r) mod N; all-gather sends chunk (i−r+1) mod N. Verify the figure arrows against a four-rank simulation.
acceptance_test: A four-rank simulation of the caption's stated algorithm produces the same send/receive chunk indices as the figure and leaves each rank with the correct reduced chunk before all-gather.
verdict_evidence: ch9 L67 caption 'In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r'; simulating N=4, rank 0 (steps 0-2: send 0/receive 3; send 3/receive 2; send 2/receive 1) ends holding chunk 1 = (r+1) mod N, and the all-gather must then send (i−r+1) mod N, not (i−r) mod N.
fix_instruction: Give the two phase-specific formulas: reduce-scatter sends chunk (i−r) mod N and leaves rank i holding reduced chunk (i+1) mod N (0-indexed rounds); all-gather sends chunk (i−r+1) mod N. Verify the Fig 9.2 arrows against an N=4 simulation.

quoted_clause: If the budget can accommodate NVLink‑equipped hosts (GPUs connected on‑node), keeping the all-reduce on-node gives an ideal ring time about 1/11th the assumed InfiniBand case and about 1/180th the assumed RoCE case (§9.3)
observed: The preceding sentence describes an eight-node data-parallel training job with one rank per node. An eight-node DP all-reduce cannot be 'kept on-node' by buying NVLink-equipped hosts; the collective is cross-host by construction. The later clarification says the ratios compare an eight-rank single-host collective with an eight-rank cross-host collective, but the earlier sentence reads as a deployment option for the same eight-node job.
correction: Rewrite the paragraph to say explicitly: 'The 1/11 and 1/180 ratios are not a fabric choice for the same eight-node job. They compare an eight-rank single-host collective with an eight-rank cross-host collective. For the eight-node job, NVLink/NVSwitch handles intra-node traffic and the inter-node fabric handles the DP all-reduce; compare InfiniBand vs Ethernet only for that inter-node portion.'
acceptance_test: A reader cannot infer that buying NVLink hosts eliminates the cross-host all-reduce in an eight-node DP job; the ratio's scope is stated before the ratio is used.
verdict_evidence: ch9 L148, after 'data-parallel training of a 70B FP16 model across 8 nodes (an eight-rank DP group, e.g. one rank per node)', says 'keeping the all-reduce on-node gives an ideal ring time about 1/11th the assumed InfiniBand case', then retracts it in the same paragraph: 'An eight-node data-parallel job uses NVLink/NVSwitch for intra-node ... The 1/11 and 1/180 ratios compare an eight-rank single-host collective with an eight-rank cross-host collective ... not two fabrics for the same job.'
fix_instruction: Delete the 'keeping the all-reduce on-node' clause and open the paragraph with what the ratios are: a single-host eight-rank collective vs a cross-host one; for the eight-node DP job the all-reduce is necessarily inter-node, so compare InfiniBand vs Ethernet only for that portion.

quoted_clause: each per-layer all-reduce is ~0.45 MB sent per rank — batch × hidden × bytes, sub-MB to a few MB
observed: The parenthetical formula 'batch × hidden × bytes' gives the logical input tensor size, not the bytes sent per rank by a ring all-reduce. For a ring, each rank sends 2(N−1)/N times the logical tensor across reduce-scatter plus all-gather, or 1.75× for N=8. With batch 16, hidden 8,192, and BF16, the logical input is 256 KiB; the ring send per rank is 448 KiB. The quoted '~0.45 MB sent per rank' is consistent with the ring send, but the formula beside it is not.
correction: Change to: 'each per-layer all-reduce has a logical input of batch × hidden × bytes; the ring send per rank is 1.75× that for an eight-rank ring, about 0.45 MB in this example.'
acceptance_test: Recomputing from the quoted formula yields the quoted sent-per-rank number, including the ring normalization.
verdict_evidence: Ch9 §8: "each per-layer all-reduce is ~0.45 MB sent per rank — batch × hidden × bytes", while Ch10 derives the same op as "logical input of M = 16 x 8,192 x 2 = 262,144 B = 256 KiB" plus "the ring moves 1.75M = 448 KiB per rank sent"; the formula omits the 2(N-1)/N = 1.75 ring factor that produces the quoted 0.45 MB (448 KiB = 0.459 MB).
fix_instruction: Rewrite the parenthetical as "1.75 x batch x hidden x bytes for an 8-rank ring (256 KiB logical -> ~0.45 MB sent per rank), sub-MB to a few MB" so the formula reproduces the quoted number.

page_hint: Chapter 9, §5 Common Mistakes, "Ignoring contention from other traffic"
quoted_clause: if other collectives (e.g., all-gather for optimizer state) are running simultaneously
observed: FSDP-style training all-gathers parameter shards, not optimizer state. Optimizer state is sharded and updated locally; it is not the object normally all-gathered.
correction: Replace with "all-gather for parameter shards (FSDP)" or "reduce-scatter for gradients".
acceptance_test: The example collective must correspond to a real FSDP/DP training communication pattern.
verdict_evidence: ch9 Common Mistakes: 'if other collectives (e.g., all-gather for optimizer state) are running simultaneously, the bisection bandwidth is shared' — but FSDP/ZeRO all-gathers parameter shards and reduce-scatters gradients; ch10 itself writes 'FSDP ... all-gathers parameter shards and ... reduce-scatters gradients'. Optimizer state is sharded and updated locally, never all-gathered.
fix_instruction: Replace the example with 'all-gather for parameter shards (FSDP) or reduce-scatter for gradients'.

observed: Caption formula '"In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r"' is internally inconsistent under any single round-indexing convention. With 0-indexed rounds (r=0,1,2) the formula is valid for both phases, but the reduce-scatter result is rank r retaining chunk (r+1) mod N — rank 0 would retain chunk 1 (sum=20), not the drawn chunk 0 (sum=10). With 1-indexed rounds (r=1,2,3) the formula produces the drawn intermediate state for reduce-scatter, but the all-gather fails: in round 1 rank 0 must send chunk (0−1)mod4=3, which it does not yet hold after reduce-scatter (it holds only chunk 0). The conclusion 'so rank r holds chunk r' only follows with 1-indexed rounds; 'both phases' only holds with 0-indexed rounds. The two claims cannot both be true simultaneously.
acceptance_test: Caption states the round-indexing convention explicitly and, under that single convention, the formula simultaneously (a) produces the drawn reduce-scatter intermediate state and (b) is valid for the all-gather starting state. Alternatively, caption gives separate formulas for the two phases.
verdict_evidence: Caption on printed 159 reads 'In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r' (PDF p179 text lines 45-46); simulation shows RS with r=0,1,2 makes rank 0 retain chunk 1 (sum 20) not the drawn chunk 0 (sum 10), while r=1,2,3 sends chunk 3 first in the all-gather which rank 0 no longer holds — the one formula cannot serve both phases.
fix_instruction: Fix the caption to state the indexing per phase, e.g. 'In round r of the reduce-scatter (r = 1…N−1) rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N and retains chunk i; in round r of the all-gather (r = 0…N−2) rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N, beginning with its own reduced chunk i.' Do not change the figure: it already matches the reduce-scatter convention.

observed: The caption's statement 'In round 1, rank i sends chunk (i-1) mod N in both phases' is correct for the reduce-scatter phase but wrong for the all-gather phase. In a ring all-gather, round 1 has rank i send its own chunk i to rank i+1; only in round 2 does it forward chunk (i-1) mod N. As written, the caption teaches the wrong chunk index for one of the two phases it is describing, and the figure's own 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' panel cannot disambiguate it because it shows only the neighbor order, not the chunk indices.
acceptance_test: Caption must state the chunk index per phase correctly, e.g. 'In reduce-scatter round 1, rank i sends chunk (i-1) mod N to rank i+1; in all-gather round 1, rank i sends its own chunk i to rank i+1'. Optionally add the chunk index to the ring panel so the figure carries the information rather than the caption alone.
verdict_evidence: Same caption sentence verified in the PDF text layer; the all-gather round-1 send of chunk (i−1) mod N is infeasible because after reduce-scatter rank i holds only chunk i, so only the reduce-scatter half of the 'both phases' claim is true (duplicate of the FIG-9.2-01 math lead).
fix_instruction: Same fix as FIG-9.2-01: split the formula by phase and state that the all-gather round 0 sends each rank's own reduced chunk.
